The angle is the total change of direction through the whole bend: 90° is a right-angle turn, 180° a hairpin. A bend also has to be tight enough; long sweeping highway bends are not curves.

Only tight ones: from 45°, radius up to ~170 m. Only bends you really have to brake for.

Normal: from 30°, radius up to ~250 m.

Also gentle ones: from 20°, radius up to ~350 m. Two bends in the same direction close together can merge into one.

All over 15°: from 16°, radius up to ~570 m. Everything except the faintest bends; bends close together stay separate. Recommended.

Arrow on the bike's display:
• Slight: under 55° and wider than 60 m radius
• Normal: 55° or more, or tighter than 60 m
• Sharp: 100° or more, or tighter than 30 m
• Hairpin (U-turn arrow): 150° or more and tighter than 35 m

KawaNav says the kind of bend and its direction, like "Sharp bend left" or "Hairpin right", about 6 seconds before the bend starts at your speed: from 50 m before it when slow up to 300 m when fast. Each bend once, and nothing below 10 km/h. Your speed is the bike's own while it is connected, which has no GPS delay; without the bike, the GPS speed.

The kinds are those of the arrow on the bike's display (see "Which curves count"):
• Hairpins only
• Sharp and hairpins
• All curves: also normal and slight bends

"Also when too fast" adds the bends you come at too fast for your pace, with "slow down"; it works also with this one off.

A bend that starts within 80 m after the end of the one said is named with it: "Hairpin left, then sharp bend right". It is not said again on its own, unless you come at it too fast.

It works with or without navigation, whatever the display shows. During navigation, a bend right before Maps' next maneuver is left to Maps' own voice. Needs downloaded roads, like the curves on the display. The voice is the phone's text-to-speech, in KawaNav's language (Settings → Appearance → Language).
Your pace is how far you lean through a bend. From the bend\'s radius in the map data it gives the speed you would take the bend at:
%1$s (%2$.0f°): %3$.0f km/h at a radius of 30 m, %4$.0f km/h at 100 m

From my rides: the lean you usually reach in a bend in your last %1$d rides, once they hold %2$d bends; Normal until then. A bend counts from %3$.0f km/h and %4$d° of lean. Needs rides recorded with the bike connected, and is worked out again each time KawaNav starts

Coming at a bend more than %1$.0f%% faster than that, you hear it with \"slow down\" (\"Bend left, slow down\") when gentle braking would only just be enough: about 0.3 g, after %2$.1f s to hear it and react. If you are slowing down enough already, nothing is said.\n\nAny kind of bend, also with \"Spoken curve warnings\" off, as long as it counts under \"Which curves count\". The radius from the map is rough, and a wide line makes a bend wider than the road: the speeds err on the careful side.

A bend is two seconds or more leant the same way by more than 10°; its apex is the second leant over the most. The radius is the one that speed and lean give in a steady turn. Braking at the apex: the throttle shut and the bike slowing by more than 0.1 g there. Tap a bend to see it on the track and the chart.
